changes.historical_text: Once per turn, during your Main Phase, you can pay 800 Life Points. If you do this, until the End Phase, Spell and Trap Cards cannot be activated.
changes.modern_text: Once per turn, during your Main Phase, you can pay 800 Life Points. If you do this, until the End Phase, Spell and Trap Cards cannot be activated.
changes.summary: Era reading of 'until the End Phase', no text difference: the goat script registers an extra EVENT_ADJUST continuous effect whose condition is `Duel.GetCurrentPhase()==PHASE_END` and whose operation resets the EFFECT_CANNOT_ACTIVATE lock, so Spell and Trap Cards become activatable as soon as that End Phase begins. The modern script leaves the lock in place until RESET_PHASE|PHASE_END fires at the end of the End Phase, so nothing can be activated during it. The other two diff lines are non-behavioural and were verified against the repo: the inline s.cost is the body of Cost.PayLP(800) minus the modern cost_lp_paid bookkeeping, and `re:IsActiveType(TYPE_SPELL+TYPE_TRAP)` is the literal body of Effect.IsSpellTrapEffect (utility.lua). Chronology is unresolved.

review.notes: CONFLICT - the packet's errata_page is 'Card Errata:Sasuke Samurai' (revid 5111881 aside, title and content), a DIFFERENT card. All four English lineage versions describe Sasuke Samurai's face-down-attacker destruction effect (PGD-015, DB2-EN216, 5DS2-EN010, LCJW-EN034), not Sasuke Samurai #2's Spell/Trap lock; the packet's own best match is 0.2692 for both the goat text and the modern text. The lineage is therefore unusable for this card, so I passed literal historical_text and modern_text copied from the packet (they are identical strings) and left both lineage indices null. Escalating so the packet can be repointed at the correct errata page for passcode 11760174, or so it can be confirmed that no such page exists. The behavioural judgement does not depend on the lineage: the goat cdb text and the pinned modern cdb text are byte-identical, so the divergence is a ruling, and only the script attests it. Nothing dates it - no text transition, no shared chronology entry covering effect-duration readings.
